<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Implement ScheduleLive components">
Implement the CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive live-context children for the Cleaner CRM Phoenix app at /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm.

FIRST: call the mcp start_task tool TWICE (sequentially), once per component, with requirement_name="implementation_file", entity_type="component", and:
1. entity_id="38ec155d-1d94-5397-8b9f-21f1a0fce169"
2. entity_id="0c6cd91b-c7f7-5173-9079-67290aecf703"
Each response is the authoritative work prompt (spec path, rules). Do the work for both. If start_task errors, tell me and proceed from the specs in .code_my_spec/spec/cleaner_crm_web/schedule_live/.

Context you need:
- The BDD specs are the acceptance contract — read ALL of test/spex/833_*/, 834_*/, 843_*/, 846_*/ first. They define routes (~p"/schedule", ~p"/schedule/plans/new", plausible cleaners/time-off sub-routes), data-test selectors ([data-test='weekly-board'], [data-test='cleaner-column-<id>'], [data-test='job-<id>'], [data-test='unassigned-jobs'], [data-test='job-<id>-cleaner-select'] with phx-change="reassign_job", [data-test='schedule-conflict-warning'], [data-test='job-<id>-start-time-input'], [data-test='job-<id>-cancel-button'], [data-test='job-<id>-ack-status'], [data-test='job-<id>-notification-channel']) and behaviors (series-wide conflict detection, availability blocks, preferred-cleaner defaults/warnings).
- This needs the CleanerCrm.Scheduling context (Job, RecurringPlan, AvailabilityBlock schemas + Recurrence + ConflictDetector modules + migration) — specs at .code_my_spec/spec/cleaner_crm/scheduling/. The Clients context already exists (lib/cleaner_crm/clients*). Audit entries table exists (audit_entries migration) — record schedule mutations via the Audit context if present, else leave TODO comments referencing story 840.
- ADRs: recurrence-and-timezones (12-week materialized horizon, tzdata, project-local recurrence), money-handling (integer cents), audit-logging. Rules in .code_my_spec/rules/ (liveview_design.md, context_design.md, schema_design.md).
- Scope everything by account via CleanerCrm.Users.Scope. Routes in the :require_authenticated_user live_session. House style: lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/account_live/*, DaisyUI classes.
- Coordinate: another agent may be concurrently finishing ClientLive files — do not modify lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/client_live/* or lib/cleaner_crm/clients*; read them for interfaces only.

Verify: mix compile clean, mix format, run `mix spex test/spex/833_schedule_recurring_cleaning_plans_with_series-wide_conflict_detection/` and `mix spex test/spex/834_dispatch_from_a_single_weekly_schedule_board/` — get as many green as the Scheduling domain allows (criteria touching notifications/audit UIs may stay red). `mix test` must show no regressions.

Final response: files implemented, spec pass/fail counts for 833 and 834, blockers. Under 200 words.
</teammate-message>

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Recurrence Engine & Timezones — project-local recurrence with materialized jobs, tzdata

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Story 833 is the product's differentiator: recurring plans with conflict detection across the entire series, not just the first visit (the named ZenMaid gap). Story 846 layers preferred-cleaner defaults onto generated visits. Cleaning cadences are simple (weekly/biweekly/every-4-weeks, fixed weekday/time), not arbitrary RFC 5545 RRULEs.

## Options Considered

- **Project-local recurrence module + materialized Job rows** — generate concrete jobs N weeks ahead (Oban cron); conflict detection becomes plain SQL over real rows.
- **RRULE library (e.g. `cocktail`)** — full RFC 5545 power we don't need; conflict detection against virtual occurrences is much harder than against rows.
- **Virtual occurrences computed on read** — no rows to detect conflicts against; breaks the core story.

## Decision

Write `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence` as project-local code generating a 12-week rolling horizon of `Job` rows from each `RecurringPlan` (extended by a daily Oban job). `ConflictDetector` runs SQL overlap queries across the whole materialized series against jobs and availability blocks. Times are stored UTC; each Company has an IANA timezone (via `tzdata` + `DateTime.shift_zone/2`) used for materialization and display, keeping visits pinned to local wall-clock across DST.

## Consequences

- Adds `tzdata` dependency and a `timezone` field on Company.
- Plan edits must reconcile already-materialized future jobs (regenerate unstarted ones, flag manually-modified ones) — this logic lives in `Scheduling` and needs careful spec coverage.
- 12-week horizon bounds conflict detection; conflicts beyond the horizon surface as the horizon rolls forward.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story833.Criterion7143Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 833 — Schedule recurring cleaning plans with series-wide conflict detection
  Criterion 7143 — A recurring plan generates a job for every occurrence in
  its series (weekly, biweekly, or monthly), not just the first.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  spex "a recurring plan generates the full series of jobs" do
    scenario "weekly plan generates the full series" do
      given_ :logged_in_owner_with_account

      given_ "a client \"Jamie Rivera\" with a property exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Jamie Rivera")
        property_path = create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client_path: client_path,
           property_id: id_from_path(property_path)
         })}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner \"Alex Morgan\" is available for assignment", context do
        cleaner_path = create_cleaner(context.conn, "Alex Morgan")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_id, id_from_path(cleaner_path))}
      end

      given_ "the owner creates a weekly cleaning plan for a property running for 8 weeks",
             context do
        {:ok, plan_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/plans/new")

        plan_live
        |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
          plan: %{
            property_id: context.property_id,
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner_id,
            recurrence: "weekly",
            start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
            occurrence_count: 8
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :plan_live, plan_live)}
      end

      when_ "the plan is saved", context do
        context.plan_live
        |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "8 jobs are created, one on each scheduled date", context do
        {:ok, _board_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert html =~ "8 jobs scheduled"
        assert length(Regex.scan(~r/data-test="job-card"/, html)) == 8

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp first_visit_date, do: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)
  defp id_from_path(path), do: path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_cleaner(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule/cleaners/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='cleaner-form']", cleaner: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

  @moduledoc """
  Story 833 — Schedule recurring cleaning plans with series-wide conflict detection
  Criterion 7148 — When every occurrence in a series is conflict-free, the
  series saves cleanly with no warnings.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  spex "a conflict-free series saves without any warnings" do
    scenario "clean series saves without warnings" do
      given_ :logged_in_owner_with_account

      given_ "a client \"Jamie Rivera\" with a property exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Jamie Rivera")
        property_path = create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client_path: client_path,
           property_id: id_from_path(property_path)
         })}
      end

      given_ "the assigned cleaner is available on every date in an 8-week weekly plan",
             context do
        cleaner_path = create_cleaner(context.conn, "Alex Morgan")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_id, id_from_path(cleaner_path))}
      end

      when_ "the owner creates the plan", context do
        {:ok, plan_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/plans/new")

        plan_live
        |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
          plan: %{
            property_id: context.property_id,
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner_id,
            recurrence: "weekly",
            start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
            occurrence_count: 8
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        plan_live
        |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "no conflicts are reported", context do
        {:ok, _board_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        refute html =~ "conflict"
        assert html =~ "8 jobs scheduled"

        {:ok, context}

      and_ "all 8 jobs are scheduled", context do
        {:ok, _board_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert length(Regex.scan(~r/data-test="job-card"/, html)) == 8

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp first_visit_date, do: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)
  defp id_from_path(path), do: path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_cleaner(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule/cleaners/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='cleaner-form']", cleaner: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared givens for Cleaner CRM BDD specs.

  Consumer spex modules pull these in with a plain Elixir `import`:

      import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

      scenario "..." do
        given_ :logged_in_owner_with_account
      end

  | Name | Produces | Requires |
  |---|---|---|
  | `:logged_in_owner_with_account` | `context.conn` (authenticated), `context.user`, `context.scope`, `context.account` | `context.conn` |
  """

  use SexySpex.Givens

  import Phoenix.ConnTest
  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

  register_given :logged_in_owner_with_account, context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture() |> Fixtures.set_password()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, login_live, _html} = live(context.conn, "/users/log-in")

    form =
      form(login_live, "#login_form_password",
        user: %{
          email: user.email,
          password: Fixtures.valid_user_password(),
          remember_me: true
        }
      )

    conn = submit_form(form, context.conn)

    {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset
  import Ecto.Query

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: integer(),
          role: :owner | :admin | :member,
          user_id: integer(),
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t(),
          user: CleanerCrm.Users.User.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          account: CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: NaiveDateTime.t(),
          updated_at: NaiveDateTime.t()
        }

  schema "members" do
    field :role, Ecto.Enum, values: [:owner, :admin, :member], default: :member

    belongs_to :user, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(member, attrs) do
    member
    |> cast(attrs, [:role, :user_id, :account_id])
    |> validate_required([:role, :user_id, :account_id])
    |> validate_inclusion(:role, [:owner, :admin, :member])
    |> assoc_constraint(:user)
    |> assoc_constraint(:account)
    |> unique_constraint([:user_id, :account_id], name: :members_user_id_account_id_index)
  end

  def update_role_changeset(member, attrs) do
    member
    |> cast(attrs, [:role])
    |> validate_required([:role])
    |> validate_inclusion(:role, [:owner, :admin, :member])
  end

  def validate_owner_exists(changeset, repo) do
    case get_field(changeset, :role) do
      :owner ->
        changeset

      _ ->
        user_id = get_field(changeset, :user_id)
        account_id = get_field(changeset, :account_id)

        if user_id && account_id do
          case repo.get_by(__MODULE__, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
            %{role: :owner} ->
              owner_count =
                repo.aggregate(
                  from(m in __MODULE__, where: m.account_id == ^account_id and m.role == :owner),
                  :count
                )

              if owner_count <= 1 do
                add_error(changeset, :role, "account must have at least one owner")
              else
                changeset
              end

            _ ->
              changeset
          end
        else
          changeset
        end
    end
  end

  def has_role?(member, required_role) do
    role_hierarchy = %{member: 1, admin: 2, owner: 3}
    Map.get(role_hierarchy, member.role, 0) >= Map.get(role_hierarchy, required_role, 0)
  end

  def owner?(member), do: member.role == :owner
  def admin_or_owner?(member), do: member.role in [:admin, :owner]
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.
4	
5	  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
6	  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
7	  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.
8	
9	  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
10	  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
11	  """
12	
13	  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]
14	
15	  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
16	  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
17	  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
18	  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
19	            [
20	              CleanerCrm.Clients,
21	              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
22	              CleanerCrm.Quality,
23	              CleanerCrm.Billing,
24	              CleanerCrm.TimeTracking,
25	              CleanerCrm.Notifications
26	            ]}
27	
28	  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
29	  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
30	  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
31	  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
32	  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
33	  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
34	  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
35	  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
36	
37	  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
38	  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
39	  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
40	  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
41	    {:ok, account} =
42	      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
43	        scope,
44	        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
45	      )
46	
47	    account
48	  end
49	
50	  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
51	  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
52	  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
53	
54	  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
55	  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
56	  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
57	  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
58	  # cleaner assignment directly.
59	  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
60	    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
61	    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
62	    user
63	  end
64	
65	  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
66	  #
67	  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
68	  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
69	  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
70	  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
71	  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
72	  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
73	  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
74	  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
75	  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
76	    {:ok, client} =
77	      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
78	        scope,
79	        Enum.into(attrs, %{
80	          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
81	          card_on_file: false
82	        })
83	      )
84	
85	    client
86	  end
87	
88	  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
89	    {:ok, job} =
90	      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
91	        scope,
92	        Enum.into(attrs, %{
93	          client_id: client.id,
94	          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
95	          status: :scheduled
96	        })
97	      )
98	
99	    job
100	  end
101	
102	  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
103	    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))
104	
105	    {:ok, _checklist} =
106	      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
107	        %{
108	          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
109	          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
110	          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
111	        },
112	        %{
113	          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
114	          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
115	          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
116	        }
117	      ])
118	
119	    job
120	  end
121	
122	  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
123	    {:ok, invoice} =
124	      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
125	        scope,
126	        Enum.into(attrs, %{
127	          job_id: job.id,
128	          amount: job.agreed_price,
129	          status: :unpaid
130	        })
131	      )
132	
133	    invoice
134	  end
135	
136	  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
137	  # job.
138	  #
139	  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
140	  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
141	  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
142	  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
143	  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
144	  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
145	  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
146	  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
147	    {:ok, time_entry} =
148	      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
149	        scope,
150	        Enum.into(attrs, %{
151	          job_id: job.id,
152	          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
153	          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
154	        })
155	      )
156	
157	    time_entry
158	  end
159	
160	  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
161	  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
162	  #
163	  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
164	  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
165	  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
166	  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
167	  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
168	  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
169	  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
170	  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
171	    {:ok, notification} =
172	      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
173	        scope,
174	        Enum.into(attrs, %{
175	          client_id: client.id,
176	          job_id: job.id,
177	          kind: :reminder,
178	          channel: :email,
179	          status: :sent,
180	          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
181	        })
182	      )
183	
184	    notification
185	  end
186	
187	  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
188	  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
189	  #
190	  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
191	  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
192	  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
193	  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
194	  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
195	  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
196	  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
197	  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
198	  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
199	  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
200	  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
201	  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
202	    {:ok, notification} =
203	      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
204	        scope,
205	        Enum.into(attrs, %{
206	          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
207	          job_id: job.id,
208	          kind: :schedule_change,
209	          channel: :push,
210	          status: :pending,
211	          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
212	          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
213	          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
214	        })
215	      )
216	
217	    notification
218	  end
219	
220	  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
221	  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
222	  #
223	  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
224	  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
225	  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
226	  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
227	  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
228	  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
229	    job =
230	      job_fixture(
231	        scope,
232	        client,
233	        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
234	      )
235	
236	    {:ok, checklist} =
237	      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
238	        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
239	        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
240	        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
241	      ])
242	
243	    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
244	  end

246	  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
247	  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.

249	  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
250	  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
251	  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
252	  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
253	  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
254	  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
255	  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
256	  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
257	  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
258	  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
259	  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
260	    job =
261	      job_fixture(
262	        scope,
263	        client,
264	        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
265	      )
266	
267	    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)
268	
269	    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
270	  end
271	end

  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Quality,
              CleanerCrm.Billing,
              CleanerCrm.TimeTracking,
              CleanerCrm.Notifications
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7167Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7167 — See the whole week at a glance: the board shows
  every cleaner's jobs for the selected week on one screen.

  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Board` (mounted at `/schedule`,
  per the project's BDD plan) renders a `[data-test='weekly-board']`
  container with one `[data-test='cleaner-column-<id>']` per cleaner,
  each containing `[data-test='job-<id>']` cards for that cleaner's
  jobs. Cleaners are seeded via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`,
  added for this story since no creation flow covers cleaner
  assignment yet.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the owner sees the whole week at a glance" do
    scenario "the board shows all 4 cleaners and their jobs across the week" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the company has 4 cleaners with jobs scheduled this week", context do
        monday = week_monday()

        {cleaners, jobs} =
          ["Ana", "Ben", "Chloe", "Dana"]
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {name, offset} ->
            cleaner =
              Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
                email:
                  "#{String.downcase(name)}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
              })

            client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "#{name}'s client"})

            job =
              Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
                cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
                scheduled_date: Date.add(monday, offset),
                start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
                end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
              })

            {cleaner, job}
          end)
          |> Enum.unzip()

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaners: cleaners, jobs: jobs})}
      end

      when_ "the owner opens the weekly board for that week", context do
        {:ok, view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :view, view)}
      end

      then_ "the board shows all 4 cleaners and their jobs across the seven days on one screen",
            context do
        assert has_element?(context.view, "[data-test='weekly-board']")

        for cleaner <- context.cleaners do
          assert has_element?(
                   context.view,
                   "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{cleaner.id}']",
                   cleaner.email
                 )
        end

        for job <- context.jobs do
          assert has_element?(context.view, "[data-test='job-#{job.id}']")
        end

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp week_monday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
  end
end

  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7170 — Reassigning a job to another cleaner on the board
  updates that job's assignment immediately.

  Assumes each job card exposes a per-job cleaner-select control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-cleaner-select']`, `phx-change="reassign_job"`)
  since drag-and-drop isn't drivable through LiveViewTest.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the owner reassigns a job to another cleaner" do
    scenario "moving a job from Ana to Ben updates the assignment" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a Wednesday job is assigned to cleaner Ana", context do
        ana =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        ben =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ben-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Wednesday client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: ana.id,
            scheduled_date: wednesday(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[15:00:00]

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{ana: ana, ben: ben, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the owner moves the job to cleaner Ben on the board", context do
        {:ok, view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        view
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cleaner-select']")

      then_ "the job's assigned cleaner becomes Ben", context do

               )

        {:ok, context}

    end

  defp wednesday do

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7173Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7173 — The board blocks assigning a job to a cleaner who
  already has an overlapping job at that time.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the board blocks a conflicting reassignment" do
    scenario "moving an overlapping job onto Ben is rejected" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "cleaner Ben already has a job from 10am to 12pm Wednesday", context do
        ana =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        ben =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ben-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        bens_client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Ben's existing client"})

        _bens_existing_job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, bens_client, %{
            cleaner_id: ben.id,
            scheduled_date: wednesday(),
            start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
          })

        anas_client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "11am client"})

        eleven_am_job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, anas_client, %{
            cleaner_id: ana.id,
            scheduled_date: wednesday(),
            start_time: ~T[11:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{ana: ana, ben: ben, job: eleven_am_job})}
      end

      when_ "the owner tries to move the 11am Wednesday job onto Ben", context do
        {:ok, view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        view
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(context.ben.id)})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :view, view)}
      end

      then_ "the board rejects the move and keeps the job on its original cleaner", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ana.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        refute has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ben.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner sees a conflict warning", context do
        assert has_element?(context.view, "[data-test='schedule-conflict-warning']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp wednesday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    monday = Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
    Date.add(monday, 2)
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
2	  use Ecto.Schema
3	  import Ecto.Changeset
4	
5	  schema "users" do
6	    field :email, :string
7	    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
8	    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
9	    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
10	    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true
11	
12	    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
13	  end
14	
15	  @doc """
16	  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.
17	
18	  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.
19	
20	  ## Options
21	
22	    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
23	      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
24	      Defaults to `true`.
25	  """
26	  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
27	    user
28	    |> cast(attrs, [:email])
29	    |> validate_email(opts)
30	  end
31	
32	  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
33	    changeset =
34	      changeset
35	      |> validate_required([:email])
36	      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
37	        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
38	      )
39	      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)
40	
41	    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
42	      changeset
43	      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
44	      |> unique_constraint(:email)
45	      |> validate_email_changed()
46	    else
47	      changeset
48	    end
49	  end
50	
51	  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
52	    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
53	      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
54	    else
55	      changeset
56	    end
57	  end
58	
59	  @doc """
60	  A user changeset for changing the password.
61	
62	  It is important to validate the length of the password, as long passwords may
63	  be very expensive to hash for certain algorithms.
64	
65	  ## Options
66	
67	    * `:hash_password` - Hashes the password so it can be stored securely
68	      in the database and ensures the password field is cleared to prevent
69	      leaks in the logs. If password hashing is not needed and clearing the
70	      password field is not desired (like when using this changeset for
71	      validations on a LiveView form), this option can be set to `false`.
72	      Defaults to `true`.
73	  """
74	  def password_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
75	    user
76	    |> cast(attrs, [:password])
77	    |> validate_confirmation(:password, message: "does not match password")
78	    |> validate_password(opts)
79	  end
80	
81	  defp validate_password(changeset, opts) do
82	    changeset
83	    |> validate_required([:password])
84	    |> validate_length(:password, min: 12, max: 72)
85	    # Examples of additional password validation:
86	    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[a-z]/, message: "at least one lower case character")
87	    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[A-Z]/, message: "at least one upper case character")
88	    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[!?@#$%^&*_0-9]/, message: "at least one digit or punctuation character")
89	    |> maybe_hash_password(opts)
90	  end
91	
92	  defp maybe_hash_password(changeset, opts) do
93	    hash_password? = Keyword.get(opts, :hash_password, true)
94	    password = get_change(changeset, :password)
95	
96	    if hash_password? && password && changeset.valid? do
97	      changeset
98	      # If using Bcrypt, then further validate it is at most 72 bytes long
99	      |> validate_length(:password, max: 72, count: :bytes)
100	      # Hashing could be done with `Ecto.Changeset.prepare_changes/2`, but that
101	      # would keep the database transaction open longer and hurt performance.
102	      |> put_change(:hashed_password, Bcrypt.hash_pwd_salt(password))
103	      |> delete_change(:password)
104	    else
105	      changeset
106	    end
107	  end
108	
109	  @doc """
110	  Confirms the account by setting `confirmed_at`.
111	  """
112	  def confirm_changeset(user) do
113	    now = DateTime.utc_now(:second)
114	    change(user, confirmed_at: now)
115	  end
116	
117	  @doc """
118	  Verifies the password.
119	
120	  If there is no user or the user doesn't have a password, we call

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  schema "users" do
    field :email, :string
    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.

  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.

  ## Options

    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:email])
    |> validate_email(opts)
  end

  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
    changeset =
      changeset
      |> validate_required([:email])
      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
      )
      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)

    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
      changeset
      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
      |> unique_constraint(:email)
      |> validate_email_changed()
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for changing the password.

  It is important to validate the length of the password, as long passwords may
  be very expensive to hash for certain algorithms.

  ## Options

    * `:hash_password` - Hashes the password so it can be stored securely
      in the database and ensures the password field is cleared to prevent
      leaks in the logs. If password hashing is not needed and clearing the
      password field is not desired (like when using this changeset for
      validations on a LiveView form), this option can be set to `false`.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def password_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:password])
    |> validate_confirmation(:password, message: "does not match password")
    |> validate_password(opts)
  end

  defp validate_password(changeset, opts) do
    changeset
    |> validate_required([:password])
    |> validate_length(:password, min: 12, max: 72)
    # Examples of additional password validation:
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[a-z]/, message: "at least one lower case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[A-Z]/, message: "at least one upper case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[!?@#$%^&*_0-9]/, message: "at least one digit or punctuation character")
    |> maybe_hash_password(opts)
  end

  defp maybe_hash_password(changeset, opts) do
    hash_password? = Keyword.get(opts, :hash_password, true)
    password = get_change(changeset, :password)

    if hash_password? && password && changeset.valid? do
      changeset
      # If using Bcrypt, then further validate it is at most 72 bytes long
      |> validate_length(:password, max: 72, count: :bytes)
      # Hashing could be done with `Ecto.Changeset.prepare_changes/2`, but that
      # would keep the database transaction open longer and hurt performance.
      |> put_change(:hashed_password, Bcrypt.hash_pwd_salt(password))
      |> delete_change(:password)
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Confirms the account by setting `confirmed_at`.
  """
  def confirm_changeset(user) do
    now = DateTime.utc_now(:second)
    change(user, confirmed_at: now)
  end

  @doc """
  Verifies the password.

  If there is no user or the user doesn't have a password, we call
  `Bcrypt.no_user_verify/0` to avoid timing attacks.
  """
  def valid_password?(%CleanerCrm.Users.User{hashed_password: hashed_password}, password)
      when is_binary(hashed_password) and byte_size(password) > 0 do
    Bcrypt.verify_pass(password, hashed_password)
  end

  def valid_password?(_, _) do
    Bcrypt.no_user_verify()
    false
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_client!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Client{account_id: account_id}
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  ## Properties

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Property{} = property,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  defp record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, property_id) do
    changed_fields =
      Property.access_code_fields()
      |> Enum.filter(&Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, &1))
      |> Enum.map(&to_string/1)

    case changed_fields do
      [] ->
        :ok

      fields ->
        Recorder.record(scope, "access_details_updated", "Property", property_id, %{}, %{
          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users do
  @moduledoc """
  The Users context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{User, UserToken, UserNotifier}

  ## Database getters

  @doc """
  Gets a user by email.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_user_by_email("foo@example.com")
      %User{}

      iex> get_user_by_email("unknown@example.com")
      nil

  """
  def get_user_by_email(email) when is_binary(email) do
    Repo.get_by(User, email: email)
  end

  @doc """
  Gets a user by email and password.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_user_by_email_and_password("foo@example.com", "correct_password")
      %User{}

      iex> get_user_by_email_and_password("foo@example.com", "invalid_password")
      nil

  """
  def get_user_by_email_and_password(email, password)
      when is_binary(email) and is_binary(password) do
    user = Repo.get_by(User, email: email)
    if User.valid_password?(user, password), do: user
  end

  @doc """
  Gets a single user.

  Raises `Ecto.NoResultsError` if the User does not exist.

  ## Examples

      iex> get_user!(123)
      %User{}

      iex> get_user!(456)
      ** (Ecto.NoResultsError)

  """
  def get_user!(id), do: Repo.get!(User, id)

  ## User registration

  @doc """
  Registers a user.

  ## Examples

      iex> register_user(%{field: value})
      {:ok, %User{}}

      iex> register_user(%{field: bad_value})
      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}}

  """
  def register_user(attrs) do
    %User{}
    |> User.email_changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Settings

  @doc """
  Checks whether the user is in sudo mode.

  The user is in sudo mode when the last authentication was done no further
  than 20 minutes ago. The limit can be given as second argument in minutes.
  """
  def sudo_mode?(user, minutes \\ -20)

  def sudo_mode?(%User{authenticated_at: ts}, minutes) when is_struct(ts, DateTime) do
    DateTime.after?(ts, DateTime.utc_now() |> DateTime.add(minutes, :minute))
  end

  def sudo_mode?(_user, _minutes), do: false

  @doc """
  Returns an `%Ecto.Changeset{}` for changing the user email.

  See `CleanerCrm.Users.User.email_changeset/3` for a list of supported options.

  ## Examples

      iex> change_user_email(user)
      %Ecto.Changeset{data: %User{}}

  """
  def change_user_email(user, attrs \\ %{}, opts \\ []) do
    User.email_changeset(user, attrs, opts)
  end

  @doc """
  Updates the user email using the given token.

  If the token matches, the user email is updated and the token is deleted.
  """
  def update_user_email(user, token) do
    context = "change:#{user.email}"

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, query} <- UserToken.verify_change_email_token_query(token, context),
           %UserToken{sent_to: email} <- Repo.one(query),
           {:ok, user} <- Repo.update(User.email_changeset(user, %{email: email})),
           {_count, _result} <-
             Repo.delete_all(from(UserToken, where: [user_id: ^user.id, context: ^context])) do
        {:ok, user}
      else
        _ -> {:error, :transaction_aborted}
      end
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Returns an `%Ecto.Changeset{}` for changing the user password.

  See `CleanerCrm.Users.User.password_changeset/3` for a list of supported options.

  ## Examples

      iex> change_user_password(user)
      %Ecto.Changeset{data: %User{}}

  """
  def change_user_password(user, attrs \\ %{}, opts \\ []) do
    User.password_changeset(user, attrs, opts)
  end

  @doc """
  Updates the user password.

  Returns a tuple with the updated user, as well as a list of expired tokens.

  ## Examples

      iex> update_user_password(user, %{password: ...})
      {:ok, {%User{}, [...]}}

      iex> update_user_password(user, %{password: "too short"})
      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}}

  """
  def update_user_password(user, attrs) do
    user
    |> User.password_changeset(attrs)
    |> update_user_and_delete_all_tokens()
  end

  ## Session

  @doc """
  Generates a session token.
  """
  def generate_user_session_token(user) do
    {token, user_token} = UserToken.build_session_token(user)
    Repo.insert!(user_token)
    token
  end

  @doc """
  Gets the user with the given signed token.

  If the token is valid `{user, token_inserted_at}` is returned, otherwise `nil` is returned.
  """
  def get_user_by_session_token(token) do
    {:ok, query} = UserToken.verify_session_token_query(token)
    Repo.one(query)
  end

  @doc """
  Gets the user with the given magic link token.
  """
  def get_user_by_magic_link_token(token) do
    with {:ok, query} <- UserToken.verify_magic_link_token_query(token),
         {user, _token} <- Repo.one(query) do
      user
    else
      _ -> nil
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user in by magic link.

  There are three cases to consider:

  1. The user has already confirmed their email. They are logged in
     and the magic link is expired.

  2. The user has not confirmed their email and no password is set.
     In this case, the user gets confirmed, logged in, and all tokens -
     including session ones - are expired. In theory, no other tokens
     exist but we delete all of them for best security practices.

  3. The user has not confirmed their email but a password is set.
     This cannot happen in the default implementation but may be the
     source of security pitfalls. See the "Mixing magic link and password registration" section of
     `mix help phx.gen.auth`.
  """
  def login_user_by_magic_link(token) do
    {:ok, query} = UserToken.verify_magic_link_token_query(token)

    case Repo.one(query) do
      # Prevent session fixation attacks by disallowing magic links for unconfirmed users with password
      {%User{confirmed_at: nil, hashed_password: hash}, _token} when not is_nil(hash) ->
        raise """
        magic link log in is not allowed for unconfirmed users with a password set!

        This cannot happen with the default implementation, which indicates that you
        might have adapted the code to a different use case. Please make sure to read the
        "Mixing magic link and password registration" section of `mix help phx.gen.auth`.
        """

      {%User{confirmed_at: nil} = user, _token} ->
        user
        |> User.confirm_changeset()
        |> update_user_and_delete_all_tokens()

      {user, token} ->
        Repo.delete!(token)
        {:ok, {user, []}}

      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc ~S"""
  Delivers the update email instructions to the given user.

  ## Examples

      iex> deliver_user_update_email_instructions(user, current_email, &url(~p"/users/settings/confirm-email/#{&1}"))
      {:ok, %{to: ..., body: ...}}

  """
  def deliver_user_update_email_instructions(%User{} = user, current_email, update_email_url_fun)
      when is_function(update_email_url_fun, 1) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = UserToken.build_email_token(user, "change:#{current_email}")

    Repo.insert!(user_token)
    UserNotifier.deliver_update_email_instructions(user, update_email_url_fun.(encoded_token))
  end

  @doc """
  Delivers the magic link login instructions to the given user.
  """
  def deliver_login_instructions(%User{} = user, magic_link_url_fun)
      when is_function(magic_link_url_fun, 1) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    Repo.insert!(user_token)
    UserNotifier.deliver_login_instructions(user, magic_link_url_fun.(encoded_token))
  end

  @doc """
  Deletes the signed token with the given context.
  """
  def delete_user_session_token(token) do
    Repo.delete_all(from(UserToken, where: [token: ^token, context: "session"]))
    :ok
  end

  ## Token helper

  defp update_user_and_delete_all_tokens(changeset) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, user} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
        tokens_to_expire = Repo.all_by(UserToken, user_id: user.id)

        Repo.delete_all(from(t in UserToken, where: t.id in ^Enum.map(tokens_to_expire, & &1.id)))

        {:ok, {user, tokens_to_expire}}
      end
    end)
  end
end
