defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.update_account(account, attrs) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:updated, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def delete_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.delete_account(account) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:deleted, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def change_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)
    Account.changeset(account, attrs)
  end

  def list_account_members(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.list_account_members(account_id)
  end

  def add_user_to_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:created, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:deleted, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:updated, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.get_user_role(user_id, account_id)
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)
  end

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Invitations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  def subscribe_invitations(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations")
  end

  defp broadcast_invitation(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations", message)
  end

  def invite_user(scope, account_id, email, role)
      when is_binary(email) and role in [:owner, :admin, :member] and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         :ok <- validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id),
         {:ok, invitation} <- create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role),
         :ok <- send_invitation_email(invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:created, invitation})
      {:ok, invitation}
    end
  end

  def accept_invitation(token, user_attrs) when is_binary(token) and is_map(user_attrs) do
    with {:ok, invitation} <- get_valid_invitation(token),
         {:ok, user} <- resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs),
         {:ok, member} <- accept_user_to_account(user, invitation),
         {:ok, _updated} <- InvitationRepository.accept(%Scope{}, invitation) do
      {:ok, {user, member}}
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account_id) do
      InvitationRepository.list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id)
    else
      []
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(_scope, nil), do: []

  def get_invitation_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token)
  end

  def cancel_invitation(scope, account_id, invitation_id)
      when is_integer(invitation_id) and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         invitation when not is_nil(invitation) <-
           InvitationRepository.get_invitation(scope, invitation_id),
         {:ok, cancelled} <- InvitationRepository.cancel(scope, invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:updated, cancelled})
      {:ok, cancelled}
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      error -> error
    end
  end

  def cleanup_expired_invitations do
    InvitationRepository.cleanup_expired_invitations(30)
    :ok
  end

  defp validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:manage_members, scope, account_id),
      do: :ok,
      else: {:error, :not_authorized}
  end

  defp validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id) do
    case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
      nil ->
        :ok

      user ->
        if MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(user.id, account_id),
          do: {:error, :user_already_member},
          else: :ok
    end
  end

  defp create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role) do
    attrs = %{
      email: email,
      role: role,
      account_id: account_id,
      invited_by_user_id: scope.user.id
    }

    InvitationRepository.create_invitation(scope, attrs)
  end

  defp send_invitation_email(invitation) do
    url = CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/invitations/accept/#{invitation.token}"

    case InvitationNotifier.deliver_invitation_email(invitation, url) do
      {:ok, _} -> :ok
      {:error, _} -> {:error, :email_delivery_failed}
    end
  end

  defp get_valid_invitation(token) do
    case InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :invalid_token}

      invitation ->
        cond do
          invitation.status != :pending -> {:error, :invalid_token}
          DateTime.compare(DateTime.utc_now(), invitation.expires_at) != :lt -> {:error, :expired_token}
          true -> {:ok, invitation}
        end
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, %{email: provided_email} = user_attrs) do
    if provided_email == invitation.email do
      case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
        nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs)
        existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
      end
    else
      {:error, :email_mismatch}
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs) do
    user_attrs_with_email = Map.put(user_attrs, :email, invitation.email)

    case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
      nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs_with_email)
      existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
    end
  end

  defp accept_user_to_account(user, invitation) do
    inviter = Users.get_user!(invitation.invited_by_user_id)
    inviter_scope = %Scope{user: inviter, active_account_id: invitation.account_id}
    add_user_to_account(inviter_scope, user.id, invitation.account_id, invitation.role)
  end
end

1	# Money Handling — integer cents, no money library
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Quotes (835), invoices/payments (836), and pay/earnings (838, 844) all handle money. Research shows pay-transparency disputes are a core cleaner pain, so amounts must never drift from float arithmetic. The product is US-only, USD-only at MVP.
8	
9	## Options Considered
10	
11	- **Integer cents in Postgres** — exact, simple, matches Stripe's amount convention.
12	- **ex_money** — multi-currency correctness we don't need; adds a dependency and custom Ecto types.
13	- **Decimal columns** — exact but invites fractional-cent ambiguity in piece-rate math.
14	
15	## Decision
16	
17	Store all monetary amounts as integer cents (`:integer` columns, `_cents` suffix). Rate math (per-sqft, hourly proration) computes in `Decimal` and rounds half-up to cents at each persisted boundary. A small `CleanerCrm.Money` formatting helper renders `$X.XX`; Stripe amounts pass through unchanged.
18	
19	## Consequences
20	
21	- Multi-currency would require a migration to ex_money later; acceptable for a US-market MVP.
22	- Rounding policy (half-up at persistence boundaries) must be stated in Quoting and TimeTracking specs so earnings and invoice totals always reconcile.

# Money Handling — integer cents, no money library

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Quotes (835), invoices/payments (836), and pay/earnings (838, 844) all handle money. Research shows pay-transparency disputes are a core cleaner pain, so amounts must never drift from float arithmetic. The product is US-only, USD-only at MVP.

## Options Considered

- **Integer cents in Postgres** — exact, simple, matches Stripe's amount convention.
- **ex_money** — multi-currency correctness we don't need; adds a dependency and custom Ecto types.
- **Decimal columns** — exact but invites fractional-cent ambiguity in piece-rate math.

## Decision

Store all monetary amounts as integer cents (`:integer` columns, `_cents` suffix). Rate math (per-sqft, hourly proration) computes in `Decimal` and rounds half-up to cents at each persisted boundary. A small `CleanerCrm.Money` formatting helper renders `$X.XX`; Stripe amounts pass through unchanged.

## Consequences

- Multi-currency would require a migration to ex_money later; acceptable for a US-market MVP.
- Rounding policy (half-up at persistence boundaries) must be stated in Quoting and TimeTracking specs so earnings and invoice totals always reconcile.

1	# Audit Trail — project-local append-only audit table
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Story 840: owners want to see who changed what and when (a direct MaidCentral user wish), including attributing automated recurring-job generation to the system. Entries must be immutable (criterion 7198) and filterable.
8	
9	## Options Considered
10	
11	- **Project-local `audit_entries` table + `Audit.Recorder`** — explicit, scoped to the events that matter, easy to attribute system actors.
12	- **paper_trail / ex_audit** — generic row-versioning; captures noise, awkward system-actor attribution, and both are lightly maintained.
13	- **Postgres triggers** — invisible to application code and hard to attribute to the acting user.
14	
15	## Decision
16	
17	Write a project-local `CleanerCrm.Audit` context: an append-only `audit_entries` table (actor_id nullable + `system` flag, action, subject type/id, old/new value maps as JSONB, company-scoped) with a `Recorder` API called explicitly from mutating context functions. No update/delete functions are exposed; a DB rule/constraint blocks UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth.
18	
19	## Consequences
20	
21	- Explicit call sites mean a mutation can forget to record; Credo local check or code review must watch for this in mutating context functions.
22	- JSONB old/new maps keep the schema stable as audited entities evolve.
23	- Retention/archival policy deferred until data volume warrants it.
24

# Audit Trail — project-local append-only audit table

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Story 840: owners want to see who changed what and when (a direct MaidCentral user wish), including attributing automated recurring-job generation to the system. Entries must be immutable (criterion 7198) and filterable.

## Options Considered

- **Project-local `audit_entries` table + `Audit.Recorder`** — explicit, scoped to the events that matter, easy to attribute system actors.
- **paper_trail / ex_audit** — generic row-versioning; captures noise, awkward system-actor attribution, and both are lightly maintained.
- **Postgres triggers** — invisible to application code and hard to attribute to the acting user.

## Decision

Write a project-local `CleanerCrm.Audit` context: an append-only `audit_entries` table (actor_id nullable + `system` flag, action, subject type/id, old/new value maps as JSONB, company-scoped) with a `Recorder` API called explicitly from mutating context functions. No update/delete functions are exposed; a DB rule/constraint blocks UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth.

## Consequences

- Explicit call sites mean a mutation can forget to record; Credo local check or code review must watch for this in mutating context functions.
- JSONB old/new maps keep the schema stable as audited entities evolve.
- Retention/archival policy deferred until data volume warrants it.

# LiveView Design Documentation Rules

## Purpose
These rules ensure consistent, complete design documentation for Phoenix LiveViews and components before implementation.

## Design System

Before building any UI, read `.code_my_spec/design/design_system.html` for the project's design system. Use the DaisyUI component classes and theme tokens defined there. Do not invent custom colors or component patterns that deviate from the design system.

## Guidelines

Keep liveviews small and focused.
Each liveview should correspond to a path. No modifying the UI implicitly without a path change.

## LiveView Design Template

### File Structure
- Place in `docs/design/my_app_web/{context}_live/`
- Name files by function: `index.md`, `show.md`, `form.md`

### Required Sections

1. **Purpose** - Single sentence/short paragraph describing what this LiveView does
2. **Route** - The URL pattern that renders this LiveView
3. **Context Access** - List the context functions this LiveView calls
4. **LiveView Structure** - Three subsections:
   - **Mount** - What happens when LiveView initializes
   - **Events** - User interactions and their handlers
   - **Template** - UI structure and components used
5. **Data Flow** - Numbered steps of the user journey
6. **Security** - Permission checks and authorization rules
7. **Real-time Updates** - PubSub subscriptions and live updates (if applicable)

## Style Guidelines

- **Be concise** - Each section should be brief but complete
- **Use bullets** - Structure information as bullet points
- **Include context calls** - Show exactly which context functions are used
- **Show code examples** - Provide HEEx usage examples for components
- **Focus on behavior** - Describe what happens, not how it's implemented
- **Consider security** - Always include permission and authorization concerns
- **Plan for real-time** - Consider PubSub integration for live updates

## Phoenix 1.8 Form Component Pattern

**Structure**: Create a single LiveView module handling both `:new` and `:edit` actions with these required elements:

1. **Module Setup**
   ```elixir
   defmodule AppWeb.ResourceLive.Form do
     use AppWeb, :live_view
     alias App.Context
     alias App.Context.Schema
   ```

2. **Required Functions**
   - `render/1` - Form template with `phx-change="validate"` and `phx-submit="save"`
   - `mount/3` - Extract `return_to` param and call `apply_action/3`
   - `apply_action/3` - Pattern match on `:new`/`:edit`, set page title, schema, and form
   - `handle_event/3` - Handle "validate" and "save" events
   - `save_resource/3` - Pattern match on action, call context create/update functions

3. **Key Patterns**
   - Use `to_form(changeset)` for form assignment
   - Handle validation with `action: :validate` on changeset errors
   - Navigate on success with `push_navigate/2`
   - Support `return_to` parameter for flexible navigation
   - Use consistent flash messages: "Resource created/updated successfully"

4. **Template Requirements**
   - Wrap in layout component with flash and current_scope
   - Include header with dynamic page title
   - Form with proper field inputs and submit/cancel buttons
   - Cancel button navigates to computed return path

This pattern ensures consistent CRUD form behavior across your Phoenix 1.8 application.

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.PropertyFormComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.PropertyFormComponent

  # Hosts the component in isolation (no router route required) so this
  # test can exercise it before the sibling ClientLive.Index/Show pages
  # exist. Forwards the component's parent notification to the test
  # process so assertions can use `assert_receive`.
  defmodule Host do
    use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

    @impl true
    def mount(_params, session, socket) do
      {:ok,
       assign(socket, %{
         test_pid: session["test_pid"],
         current_scope: session["scope"],
         action: session["action"],
         client: session["client"],
         property: session["property"]
       })}
    end

    @impl true
    def render(assigns) do
      ~H"""
      <.live_component
        module={PropertyFormComponent}
        id="property-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@action}
        client={@client}
        property={@property}
      />
      """
    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({PropertyFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  describe "creating a property with no preselected client" do
    test "renders a client picker listing the account's clients" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Priya Nair"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{
          "scope" => scope,
          "action" => :new,
          "client" => nil,
          "property" => %Property{}
        })

      assert html =~ "Priya Nair"
    end

    test "rejects a submission with no client selected" do
      scope = scope_fixture()

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{
          "scope" => scope,
          "action" => :new,
          "client" => nil,
          "property" => %Property{}
        })

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{service_address: "123 Oak St"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='property-form']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='client-error']", "is required")
    end

    test "creates the property once a client is selected" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Priya Nair"})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{
          "scope" => scope,
          "action" => :new,
          "client" => nil,
          "property" => %Property{}
        })

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']",
        property: %{client_id: client.id, service_address: "77 Maple Ave"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = property}}
      assert property.client_id == client.id
      assert property.service_address == "77 Maple Ave"
    end
  end

  describe "creating a property under a preselected client" do
    test "does not render a client picker" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{
          "scope" => scope,
          "action" => :new,
          "client" => client,
          "property" => %Property{}
        })

      refute html =~ "Select a client"
    end

    test "rejects a blank service address" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{
          "scope" => scope,
          "action" => :new,
          "client" => client,
          "property" => %Property{}
        })

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{service_address: ""})
      |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='property-form']")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='service-address-error']", "is required")
    end

    test "saves the property with its access details and notifies the parent" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Devon Ashe"})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{
          "scope" => scope,
          "action" => :new,
          "client" => client,
          "property" => %Property{}
        })

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']",
        property: %{
          service_address: "77 Maple Ave",
          lockbox_code: "4821",
          parking_notes: "driveway only",
          pet_notes: "dog in yard"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = property}}
      assert property.client_id == client.id
      assert property.service_address == "77 Maple Ave"
      assert property.lockbox_code == "4821"
      assert property.parking_notes == "driveway only"
      assert property.pet_notes == "dog in yard"
    end
  end

  describe "editing an existing property" do
    test "preserves untouched fields and updates only the submitted ones" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)

      property =
        property_fixture(scope, client, %{
          service_address: "45 Elm St",
          lockbox_code: "4821"
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{
          "scope" => scope,
          "action" => :edit,
          "client" => client,
          "property" => property
        })

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{lockbox_code: "9077"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = updated}}
      assert updated.service_address == "45 Elm St"
      assert updated.lockbox_code == "9077"
    end

    test "records an audit entry naming the changed field, without the code value" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client, %{alarm_code: "1234"})

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{
          "scope" => scope,
          "action" => :edit,
          "client" => client,
          "property" => property
        })

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: %{alarm_code: "5678"})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {PropertyFormComponent, {:saved, %Property{} = updated}}
      assert updated.alarm_code == "5678"

      entry = Repo.get_by!(AuditEntry, subject_id: updated.id, subject_type: "Property")
      assert entry.action == "access_details_updated"
      assert entry.actor_id == scope.user.id
      assert entry.new_value["changed_fields"] == ["alarm_code"]
      refute entry.new_value["changed_fields"] |> to_string() =~ "5678"
    end
  end
end

10	  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
11	  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
12	  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
13	  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
14	  @remember_me_options [
15	    sign: true,
16	    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
17	    same_site: "Lax"
18	  ]
19	
20	  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
21	  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
22	  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
23	  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
24	  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
25	  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
26	  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
27	  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7
28	
29	  @doc """
30	  Logs the user in.
31	
32	  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
33	  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
34	  """
35	  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
36	    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)
37	
38	    conn
39	    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
40	    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
41	  end
42	
43	  @doc """
44	  Logs the user out.
45	
46	  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
47	  """
48	  def log_out_user(conn) do
49	    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
50	    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)
51	
52	    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
53	      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
54	    end
55	
56	    conn
57	    |> renew_session(nil)
58	    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
59	    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
60	  end
61	
62	  @doc """
63	  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.
64	
65	  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
66	  """
67	  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
68	    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
69	         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
70	      conn
71	      |> assign(:current_scope, Scope.for_user(user))
72	      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
73	    else
74	      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
75	    end
76	  end
77	
78	  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
79	    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
80	      {token, conn}
81	    else
82	      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])
83	
84	      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
85	        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
86	      else
87	        nil
88	      end
89	    end
90	  end

92	  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
93	  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
94	    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)
95	
96	    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
97	      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
98	    else
99	      conn
100	    end
101	  end

103	  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
104	  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
105	  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
106	  # will soon expire.
107	  #
108	  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
109	  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
110	  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
111	  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
112	    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
113	    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)
114	
115	    conn
116	    |> renew_session(user)
117	    |> put_token_in_session(token)
118	    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)

121	  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
122	  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
123	  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
124	    conn
125	  end

127	  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
128	  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
129	  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
130	  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
131	  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
132	  #
133	  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
134	  #       delete_csrf_token()
135	  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
136	  #
137	  #       conn
138	  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
139	  #       |> clear_session()
140	  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
141	  #     end
142	  #
143	  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
144	    delete_csrf_token()
145	
146	    conn
147	    |> configure_session(renew: true)
148	    |> clear_session()
149	  end

152	    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)
153

158

160	    conn

162	    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
163	  end

173	  """

182	  @doc """
183	  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.
184	
185	  ## `on_mount` arguments
186	
187	    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
188	      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
189	      there's no user_token or no matching user.
190	
191	    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
192	      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
193	      on user_token.
194	      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.
195	
196	  ## Examples

201	      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do

222	      {:cont, socket}
223	    else

242	        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, Scope.for_user(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}
    else
      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])

      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)

    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
    else
      conn
    end
  end

  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
  # will soon expire.
  #
  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
    conn
  end

  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
  #
  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
  #       delete_csrf_token()
  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
  #
  #       conn
  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
  #       |> clear_session()
  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
  #     end
  #
  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
    delete_csrf_token()

    conn
    |> configure_session(renew: true)
    |> clear_session()
  end

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn

  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
  end

  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
  end

  @doc """
  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
  """
  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
    end)
  end

  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"

  @doc """
  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.

  ## `on_mount` arguments

    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
      there's no user_token or no matching user.

    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
      on user_token.
      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.

  ## Examples

  Use the `on_mount` lifecycle macro in LiveViews to mount or authenticate
  the `current_scope`:

      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do
        use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

        on_mount {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}
        ...
      end

  Or use the `live_session` of your router to invoke the on_mount callback:

      live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
      end
  """
  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
  end

  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp mount_current_scope(socket, session) do
    Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :current_scope, fn ->
      {user, _} =
        if user_token = session["user_token"] do
          Users.get_user_by_session_token(user_token)
        end || {nil, nil}

      Scope.for_user(user)
    end)
  end

  @doc "Returns the path to redirect to after log in."
  # the user was already logged in, redirect to settings
  def signed_in_path(%Plug.Conn{assigns: %{current_scope: %Scope{user: %Users.User{}}}}) do
    ~p"/users/settings"
  end

  def signed_in_path(_), do: ~p"/"

  @doc """
  Plug for routes that require the user to be authenticated.
  """
  def require_authenticated_user(conn, _opts) do
    if conn.assigns.current_scope && conn.assigns.current_scope.user do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
      |> maybe_store_return_to()
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(%{method: "GET"} = conn) do
    put_session(conn, :user_return_to, current_path(conn))
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(conn), do: conn
end

Account Details

<.form for={@account_form} id="account-form" phx-change="validate-account" phx-submit="update-account" >
<.input field={@account_form[:name]} type="text" label="Account Name" placeholder="Enter account name" />

""" end @impl true def mount(%{"id" => id}, _session, socket) do current_scope = socket.assigns.current_scope case Accounts.get_account(current_scope, id) do nil -> {:ok, socket |> put_flash(:error, "Account not found") |> redirect(to: ~p"/accounts")} account -> Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "account:#{account.id}") {:ok, socket |> assign(:account, account) |> assign(:account_form, to_form(Account.changeset(account, %{})))} end end @impl true def handle_event("validate-account", %{"account" => account_params}, socket) do changeset = Account.changeset(socket.assigns.account, account_params) {:noreply, assign(socket, :account_form, to_form(changeset, action: :validate))} end @impl true def handle_event("update-account", %{"account" => account_params}, socket) do case Accounts.update_account( socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.account, account_params ) do {:ok, account} -> {:noreply, socket |> put_flash(:info, "Account updated successfully") |> assign(:account, account) |> assign(:account_form, to_form(Account.changeset(account, %{})))} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :account_form, to_form(changeset))} end end @impl true def handle_event("delete-account", _params, socket) do case Accounts.delete_account(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.account) do {:ok, _account} -> {:noreply, socket |> put_flash(:info, "Account deleted successfully") |> redirect(to: ~p"/accounts")} {:error, _reason} -> {:noreply, socket |> put_flash(:error, "Failed to delete account")} end end @impl true def handle_info({:account_updated, account}, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :account, account)} end defp can_delete_account?(current_scope, account) do Authorization.authorize(:delete_account, current_scope, account.id) end end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository do
  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, Member}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  def add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    %Member{}
    |> Member.changeset(%{user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id, role: role})
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        case member.role do
          :owner ->
            owner_count = count_owners(account_id)
            if owner_count > 1, do: Repo.delete(member), else: {:error, :last_owner}

          _ ->
            Repo.delete(member)
        end
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        changeset = Member.update_role_changeset(member, %{role: role})
        validated_changeset = Member.validate_owner_exists(changeset, Repo)

        case validated_changeset.valid? do
          true -> Repo.update(validated_changeset)
          false -> {:error, validated_changeset}
        end
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> nil
      member -> member.role
    end
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(user_id, account_id) do
    Repo.exists?(from m in Member, where: m.user_id == ^user_id and m.account_id == ^account_id)
  end

  def can_add_user_to_account?(_account_id), do: true

  def count_account_users(account_id) do
    Repo.aggregate(from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id), :count)
  end

  def list_user_accounts(user_id) do
    from(a in Account,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.account_id == a.id,
      where: m.user_id == ^user_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_account_users(account_id) do
    from(u in User,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.user_id == u.id,
      where: m.account_id == ^account_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_account_members(account_id) do
    from(m in Member,
      where: m.account_id == ^account_id,
      preload: [:user]
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_accounts_with_role(user_id, role) do
    from(a in Account,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.account_id == a.id,
      where: m.user_id == ^user_id and m.role == ^role
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def by_user(user_id), do: from(m in Member, where: m.user_id == ^user_id)
  def by_account(account_id), do: from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id)
  def by_role(role), do: from(m in Member, where: m.role == ^role)
  def with_user_preloads, do: from(m in Member, preload: [:user])
  def with_account_preloads, do: from(m in Member, preload: [:account])

  defp count_owners(account_id) do
    Repo.aggregate(
      from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id and m.role == :owner),
      :count
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder do
  @moduledoc """
  API other contexts call to append audit trail entries.

  Callers pass the acting scope, an action string, the subject being
  changed, and old/new value maps. Nothing here ever updates or deletes
  a row — this module only ever inserts.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Records an audit entry attributed to the scope's current user.
  """
  def record(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        action,
        subject_type,
        subject_id,
        old_value \\ %{},
        new_value \\ %{}
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(action) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    %AuditEntry{}
    |> AuditEntry.changeset(%{
      account_id: account_id,
      actor_id: scope.user && scope.user.id,
      system: false,
      action: action,
      subject_type: subject_type,
      subject_id: subject_id,
      old_value: old_value,
      new_value: new_value
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries for a subject, most recent first.
  """
  def list_for_subject(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, subject_type, subject_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    AuditEntry
    |> where(
      [e],
      e.account_id == ^account_id and e.subject_type == ^subject_type and
        e.subject_id == ^subject_id
    )
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Repo.Migrations.CreateAuditEntriesTable do
  use Ecto.Migration

  def change do
    create table(:audit_entries, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :actor_id, references(:users, on_delete: :nilify_all)
      add :system, :boolean, null: false, default: false
      add :action, :string, null: false
      add :subject_type, :string, null: false
      add :subject_id, :binary_id, null: false
      add :old_value, :map, null: false, default: %{}
      add :new_value, :map, null: false, default: %{}

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)
    end

    create index(:audit_entries, [:account_id])
    create index(:audit_entries, [:subject_type, :subject_id])

    # Defense in depth: audit entries are append-only. Application code
    # never exposes update/delete; these rules block it even if it did.
    execute(
      "CREATE RULE audit_entries_no_update AS ON UPDATE TO audit_entries DO INSTEAD NOTHING",
      "DROP RULE IF EXISTS audit_entries_no_update ON audit_entries"
    )

    execute(
      "CREATE RULE audit_entries_no_delete AS ON DELETE TO audit_entries DO INSTEAD NOTHING",
      "DROP RULE IF EXISTS audit_entries_no_delete ON audit_entries"
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines test helpers for creating
  entities via the `CleanerCrm.Users` context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def unique_user_email, do: "user#{System.unique_integer()}@example.com"
  def valid_user_password, do: "hello world!"

  def valid_user_attributes(attrs \\ %{}) do
    Enum.into(attrs, %{
      email: unique_user_email()
    })
  end

  def unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, user} =
      attrs
      |> valid_user_attributes()
      |> Users.register_user()

    user
  end

  def user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs)

    token =
      extract_user_token(fn url ->
        Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, url)
      end)

    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

    user
  end

  def user_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    user_scope_fixture(user)
  end

  def user_scope_fixture(user) do
    Scope.for_user(user)
  end

  def set_password(user) do
    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: valid_user_password()})

    user
  end

  def extract_user_token(fun) do
    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
    token
  end

  def override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) when is_binary(token) do
    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(t in Users.UserToken,
        where: t.token == ^token
      ),
      set: [authenticated_at: authenticated_at]
    )
  end

  def generate_user_magic_link_token(user) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = Users.UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    CleanerCrm.Repo.insert!(user_token)
    {encoded_token, user_token.token}
  end

  def offset_user_token(token, amount_to_add, unit) do
    dt = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(:second), amount_to_add, unit)

    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(ut in Users.UserToken, where: ut.token == ^token),
      set: [inserted_at: dt, authenticated_at: dt]
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t(),
          slug: String.t() | nil,
          members: [CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          users: [CleanerCrm.Users.User.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api www help support docs blog)

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "accounts" do
    field :name, :string
    field :slug, :string

    has_many :members, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member, on_delete: :delete_all
    has_many :users, through: [:members, :user]

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(account, attrs) do
    account
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :slug])
    |> validate_required([:name])
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 100)
    |> validate_slug()
    |> unique_constraint(:slug)
  end

  def create_changeset(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> changeset(attrs)
    |> maybe_generate_slug()
  end

  defp validate_slug(changeset) do
    changeset
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z0-9-]+$/,
      message: "must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens"
    )
    |> validate_length(:slug, min: 3, max: 50)
    |> validate_exclusion(:slug, @reserved_slugs, message: "is reserved and cannot be used")
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z]/, message: "must start with a letter")
  end

  defp maybe_generate_slug(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :slug) do
      nil ->
        name = get_field(changeset, :name)
        if name, do: put_change(changeset, :slug, generate_slug(name)), else: changeset

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_slug(name) do
    name
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]/, "-")
    |> String.replace(~r/-+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  schema "users" do
    field :email, :string
    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.

  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.

  ## Options

    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:email])
    |> validate_email(opts)
  end

  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
    changeset =
      changeset
      |> validate_required([:email])
      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
      )
      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)

    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
      changeset
      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
      |> unique_constraint(:email)
      |> validate_email_changed()
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for changing the password.

  It is important to validate the length of the password, as long passwords may
  be very expensive to hash for certain algorithms.

  ## Options

    * `:hash_password` - Hashes the password so it can be stored securely
      in the database and ensures the password field is cleared to prevent
      leaks in the logs. If password hashing is not needed and clearing the
      password field is not desired (like when using this changeset for
      validations on a LiveView form), this option can be set to `false`.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def password_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:password])
    |> validate_confirmation(:password, message: "does not match password")
    |> validate_password(opts)
  end

  defp validate_password(changeset, opts) do
    changeset
    |> validate_required([:password])
    |> validate_length(:password, min: 12, max: 72)
    # Examples of additional password validation:
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[a-z]/, message: "at least one lower case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[A-Z]/, message: "at least one upper case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[!?@#$%^&*_0-9]/, message: "at least one digit or punctuation character")
    |> maybe_hash_password(opts)
  end

  defp maybe_hash_password(changeset, opts) do
    hash_password? = Keyword.get(opts, :hash_password, true)
    password = get_change(changeset, :password)

    if hash_password? && password && changeset.valid? do
      changeset
      # If using Bcrypt, then further validate it is at most 72 bytes long
      |> validate_length(:password, max: 72, count: :bytes)
      # Hashing could be done with `Ecto.Changeset.prepare_changes/2`, but that
      # would keep the database transaction open longer and hurt performance.
      |> put_change(:hashed_password, Bcrypt.hash_pwd_salt(password))
      |> delete_change(:password)
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Confirms the account by setting `confirmed_at`.
  """
  def confirm_changeset(user) do
    now = DateTime.utc_now(:second)
    change(user, confirmed_at: now)
  end

  @doc """
  Verifies the password.

  If there is no user or the user doesn't have a password, we call
  `Bcrypt.no_user_verify/0` to avoid timing attacks.
  """
  def valid_password?(%CleanerCrm.Users.User{hashed_password: hashed_password}, password)
      when is_binary(hashed_password) and byte_size(password) > 0 do
    Bcrypt.verify_pass(password, hashed_password)
  end

  def valid_password?(_, _) do
    Bcrypt.no_user_verify()

  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan do
  @moduledoc """
  A weekly/biweekly/monthly cadence for a property that materializes a
  series of `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job` rows (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`).

  `cleaner_id` is the client's *preferred* cleaner (story 846): every
  job generated from this plan defaults to this cleaner, and
  reassigning a single visit away from them is a warning, not a block.
  It is optional — a plan with no preferred cleaner generates
  unassigned jobs and never warns on reassignment.

  `start_time`/`end_time` default to a plain 9am-11am visit window;
  nothing in the plan form asks for these explicitly today, but every
  generated job needs a concrete time to run conflict detection
  against.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurrence: :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly | nil,
          start_date: Date.t() | nil,
          occurrence_count: integer() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "recurring_plans" do
    field :recurrence, Ecto.Enum, values: [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly]
    field :start_date, :date
    field :occurrence_count, :integer
    field :start_time, :time, default: ~T[09:00:00]
    field :end_time, :time, default: ~T[11:00:00]

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(property_id cleaner_id recurrence start_date occurrence_count start_time end_time)a

  @doc """
  Changeset for the fully-specified plan a save requires.
  """
  def changeset(plan, attrs) do
    plan
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:property_id, :recurrence, :start_date, :occurrence_count])
    |> validate_number(:occurrence_count, greater_than: 0)
  end

  @doc """
  Changeset for the live preview as the owner fills in the form —
  every field is optional so the conflict list can update incrementally
  as soon as enough of them are present, well before the plan is valid
  enough to save.
  """
  def preview_changeset(plan, attrs) do
    cast(plan, attrs, @fields)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence do
  @moduledoc """
  Generates the dates for a plan's series from its cadence.

  Project-local, calendar-date arithmetic (see the recurrence ADR) —
  no RRULE library, no virtual occurrences. `:weekly` steps 7 days,
  `:biweekly` 14, `:monthly` 28 (a fixed 4-week cadence, not a calendar
  month, so the weekday never drifts).

  TODO: the recurrence ADR calls for materializing against each
  account's IANA timezone (via `tzdata`) so visits stay pinned to local
  wall-clock across DST, plus a rolling 12-week horizon extended by a
  daily Oban job. Neither is implemented yet — dates here are naive
  and every plan is materialized in full up front, bounded only by its
  own `occurrence_count`.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan

  @step_days %{weekly: 7, biweekly: 14, monthly: 28}

  @doc """
  Returns a list of `%{index:, date:}` maps, one per occurrence, in
  series order starting at 1. `nil` if the plan is missing any of the
  fields a series needs.
  """
  def occurrences(%RecurringPlan{
        recurrence: recurrence,
        start_date: %Date{} = start_date,
        occurrence_count: count
      })
      when recurrence in [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly] and is_integer(count) and count > 0 do
    step = Map.fetch!(@step_days, recurrence)

    for index <- 1..count do
      %{index: index, date: Date.add(start_date, (index - 1) * step)}
    end
  end

  def occurrences(_incomplete_plan), do: []

  @doc """
  Job attribute maps ready for `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job/2`, one
  per occurrence.
  """
  def job_attrs(%RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    Enum.map(occurrences(plan), fn %{date: date} ->
      %{
        property_id: plan.property_id,
        cleaner_id: plan.cleaner_id,
        recurring_plan_id: plan.id,
        scheduled_date: date,
        start_time: plan.start_time,
        end_time: plan.end_time
      }
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.ConflictDetector do
  @moduledoc """
  Detects scheduling conflicts against a cleaner's availability blocks
  and already-booked jobs — for a single proposed assignment, or across
  every occurrence in a (possibly still-unsaved) recurring series.

  Two distinct reasons, surfaced separately so the UI can say something
  useful:

    * `:unavailable` — the cleaner has a time-off block covering the slot
    * `:overlap` — the cleaner already has another job booked then

  Availability is checked first: a time-off block is the more specific
  reason when both happen to apply.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{AvailabilityBlock, Job}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Checks one proposed (cleaner, date, time window) assignment.

  `exclude_job_id` omits a job (the one being reassigned) from the
  overlap check against itself. Returns `:ok` when the cleaner is
  `nil` — an unassigned job never conflicts.
  """
  def check_assignment(scope, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, exclude_job_id \\ nil)

  def check_assignment(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        cleaner_id,
        %Date{} = date,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        exclude_job_id
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and not is_nil(cleaner_id) do
    cond do
      unavailable?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) ->
        {:error, :unavailable}

      overlaps_existing_job?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, exclude_job_id) ->
        {:error, :overlap}

      true ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  def check_assignment(_scope, nil, _date, _start_time, _end_time, _exclude_job_id), do: :ok

  Detects scheduling conflicts against a cleaner's availability blocks
  and already-booked jobs — for a single proposed assignment, or across
  every occurrence in a (possibly still-unsaved) recurring series.

  Two distinct reasons, surfaced separately so the UI can say something
  useful:

    * `:unavailable` — the cleaner has a time-off block covering the slot
    * `:overlap` — the cleaner already has another job booked then

  Availability is checked first: a time-off block is the more specific
  reason when both happen to apply.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{AvailabilityBlock, Job}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  overlap check against itself. Returns `:ok` when the cleaner is
  `nil` — an unassigned job never conflicts.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Authorization do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def authorize(action, %Scope{} = scope, resource) do
    case {action, resource} do
      {:read_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)

      {:manage_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:manage_members, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:delete_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role == :owner

      _ ->
        false
    end
  end

  def authorize!(action, scope, resource) do
    unless authorize(action, scope, resource) do
      raise "Unauthorized: #{action} on #{inspect(resource)}"
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{AvailabilityBlock, ConflictDetector, Job, Recurrence, RecurringPlan}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    plan
    |> Recurrence.occurrences()
    |> then(
      &ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan.cleaner_id, &1, plan.start_time, plan.end_time)
    )
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end
