defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}
    else
      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])

      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)

    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
    else
      conn
    end
  end

  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
  # will soon expire.
  #
  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
    conn
  end

  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
  #
  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
  #       delete_csrf_token()
  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
  #
  #       conn
  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
  #       |> clear_session()
  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
  #     end
  #
  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
    delete_csrf_token()

    conn
    |> configure_session(renew: true)
    |> clear_session()
  end

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn

  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
  end

  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
  end

  @doc """
  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
  """
  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
    end)
  end

  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"

  @doc """
  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.

  ## `on_mount` arguments

    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
      there's no user_token or no matching user.

    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
      on user_token.
      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.

  ## Examples

  Use the `on_mount` lifecycle macro in LiveViews to mount or authenticate
  the `current_scope`:

      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do
        use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

        on_mount {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}
        ...
      end

  Or use the `live_session` of your router to invoke the on_mount callback:

      live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
      end
  """
  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
  end

  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp mount_current_scope(socket, session) do
    Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :current_scope, fn ->
      {user, _} =
        if user_token = session["user_token"] do
          Users.get_user_by_session_token(user_token)
        end || {nil, nil}

      scope_with_active_account(user)
    end)
  end

  # There's no persisted "current account" selection yet (the account
  # picker doesn't write one anywhere), so every account-scoped page
  # would otherwise see a permanently nil `active_account_id`. Until
  # that selection is persisted, default a signed-in user onto one of
  # their accounts — the common case is a single-account owner, for
  # whom this is unambiguous.
  defp scope_with_active_account(nil), do: Scope.for_user(nil)

  defp scope_with_active_account(user) do
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  @doc "Returns the path to redirect to after log in."
  # the user was already logged in, redirect to settings
  def signed_in_path(%Plug.Conn{assigns: %{current_scope: %Scope{user: %Users.User{}}}}) do
    ~p"/users/settings"
  end

  def signed_in_path(_), do: ~p"/"

  @doc """
  Plug for routes that require the user to be authenticated.
  """
  def require_authenticated_user(conn, _opts) do
    if conn.assigns.current_scope && conn.assigns.current_scope.user do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
      |> maybe_store_return_to()
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(%{method: "GET"} = conn) do
    put_session(conn, :user_return_to, current_path(conn))
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(conn), do: conn
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.CleanerLive do
  @moduledoc """
  Adds a cleaner to the account's roster by name, so jobs and time off
  can be assigned to them.

  Not one of the schedule live-context's tracked components (only
  `Board`, `PlanFormComponent`, and `JobFormComponent` are) — added as
  minimal supporting scaffolding because every story 833 scenario
  needs a cleaner to exist first. See
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3` for the fuller,
  login-capable path other stories seed cleaners through.
  """

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{AvailabilityBlock, ConflictDetector, Job, Recurrence, RecurringPlan}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    plan
    |> Recurrence.occurrences()
    |> then(
      &ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan.cleaner_id, &1, plan.start_time, plan.end_time)
    )
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

""" use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent @impl true def render(%{live_action: :show} = assigns) do ~H""" <.header>Job Details

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    plan
    |> Recurrence.occurrences()
    |> then(
      &ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan.cleaner_id, &1, plan.start_time, plan.end_time)
    )
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent

  # Hosts the component in isolation (no router route required), same
  # pattern as ClientLive.PropertyFormComponentTest. Forwards the
  # component's parent notification to the test process so assertions
  # can use `assert_receive`.
  defmodule Host do
    use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

    @impl true
    def mount(_params, session, socket) do
      {:ok,
       assign(socket, %{
         test_pid: session["test_pid"],
         current_scope: session["scope"],
         action: session["action"],
         job: session["job"]
       })}
    end

    @impl true
    def render(assigns) do
      ~H"""
      <.live_component
        module={JobFormComponent}
        id="job-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@action}
        job={@job}
      />
      """
    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({JobFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  describe "creating a job" do
    test "renders the job form with the account's properties" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      assert html =~ "12 Oak Lane"
      assert html =~ "job-form"
    end

    test "creates an unassigned job and notifies the parent" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
        job: %{
          property_id: property.id,
          date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
          start_time: "09:00",
          end_time: "11:00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, %Job{} = job}}
      assert job.property_id == property.id
      assert job.cleaner_id == nil
      assert job.start_time == ~T[09:00:00]
    end

    test "creates a job pre-assigned to a cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
        job: %{
          property_id: property.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
          start_time: "10:00",
          end_time: "12:00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, %Job{} = job}}
      assert job.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "rejects a submission missing the required date" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{property_id: property.id, date: "", start_time: "09:00", end_time: "11:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='job-form']")
      assert html =~ "can't be blank" or html =~ "is required"
    end
  end

  describe "assigning a cleaner to an existing job" do
    test "renders the assignment form" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      job = job_fixture(scope, property)

      {:ok, _lv, html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      assert html =~ "assignment-form"
    end

    test "assigns the cleaner when there is no conflict" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: next_tuesday(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, %Job{} = updated}}
      assert updated.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when the cleaner has a time-off block that day" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      friday = next_friday()

      availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, %{date: friday, all_day: true})

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: friday,
          start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "conflict"
      assert html =~ "unavailable"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when it overlaps another booking for that cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      booking_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)

      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: booking_date,
        start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
      })

      second_job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: booking_date,
          start_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[13:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => second_job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "overlap"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end
  end

  defp next_tuesday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    offset = Integer.mod(2 - Date.day_of_week(today) - 1, 7) + 1
    Date.add(today, offset + 7)
  end

  defp next_friday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    offset = Integer.mod(5 - Date.day_of_week(today) - 1, 7) + 1
    Date.add(today, offset + 7)
  end
end

<.header>{form_title(@action)} <.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="plan-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:property_id]} type="select" label="Property" prompt="Select a property" options={property_options(@properties)} /> <.input field={@form[:cleaner_id]} type="select" label="Preferred Cleaner" prompt="No preferred cleaner" options={cleaner_options(@cleaners)} /> <.input field={@form[:recurrence]} type="select" label="Recurrence" prompt="Select a cadence" options={[{"Weekly", "weekly"}, {"Biweekly", "biweekly"}, {"Every 4 weeks", "monthly"}]} /> <.input field={@form[:start_date]} type="date" label="Start Date" /> <.input field={@form[:occurrence_count]} type="number" label="Number of Visits" min="1" />
Visit {conflict.index} ({conflict.date}) has a scheduling conflict: {conflict_reason_text( conflict.reason )}. <.button type="button" data-test={"override-conflict-#{conflict.index}"} phx-target={@myself} phx-click="override_conflict" phx-value-index={conflict.index} > Override
<.button data-test="save-plan-button" phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Plan
""" end @impl true def update(%{plan: plan} = assigns, socket) do changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:overridden, MapSet.new()) |> assign(:properties, list_properties(assigns.current_scope)) |> assign(:cleaners, Scheduling.list_cleaners(assigns.current_scope)) |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} end @impl Phoenix.Component.update(:overridden, &MapSet.put(&1, index)) |> Phoenix.Component.update(:conflicts, &Enum.reject(&1, fn conflict -> conflict.index == index end))} end def handle_event("save", %{"plan" => params}, socket) do case Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} -> notify_parent({:saved, plan}) changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:plan, plan) |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan))} end end defp assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset) do draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) conflicts = ^account_id) |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) |> Repo.all() end defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) defp conflict_reason_text(:unavailable), do: "the cleaner is unavailable that day" defp conflict_reason_text(:overlap), do: "it overlaps another booking" defp form_title(:new), do: "New Recurring Plan" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Recurring Plan" end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.ConflictDetector do
  @moduledoc """
  Detects scheduling conflicts against a cleaner's availability blocks
  and already-booked jobs — for a single proposed assignment, or across
  every occurrence in a (possibly still-unsaved) recurring series.

  Two distinct reasons, surfaced separately so the UI can say something
  useful:

    * `:unavailable` — the cleaner has a time-off block covering the slot
    * `:overlap` — the cleaner already has another job booked then

  Availability is checked first: a time-off block is the more specific
  reason when both happen to apply.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{AvailabilityBlock, Job}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Checks one proposed (cleaner, date, time window) assignment.

  `exclude_job_id` omits a job (the one being reassigned) from the
  overlap check against itself. Returns `:ok` when the cleaner is
  `nil` — an unassigned job never conflicts.
  """
  def check_assignment(scope, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, exclude_job_id \\ nil)

  def check_assignment(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        cleaner_id,
        %Date{} = date,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        exclude_job_id
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and not is_nil(cleaner_id) do
    cond do
      unavailable?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) ->
        {:error, :unavailable}

      overlaps_existing_job?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, exclude_job_id) ->
        {:error, :overlap}

      true ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  def check_assignment(_scope, nil, _date, _start_time, _end_time, _exclude_job_id), do: :ok

  @doc """
  Checks every occurrence of a proposed series (`[%{index:, date:}, ...]`,
  as returned by `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.occurrences/1`)
  against a single cleaner, using the same visit window for each.
  Returns only the conflicting occurrences, as
  `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def check_occurrences(scope, cleaner_id, occurrences, start_time \\ ~T[09:00:00], end_time \\ ~T[11:00:00])

  def check_occurrences(_scope, nil, _occurrences, _start_time, _end_time), do: []

  def check_occurrences(scope, cleaner_id, occurrences, start_time, end_time) do
    occurrences
    |> Enum.map(fn %{index: index, date: date} ->
      case check_assignment(scope, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) do
        :ok -> nil
        {:error, reason} -> %{index: index, date: date, reason: reason}
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
  end

  defp unavailable?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) do
    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where(
      [b],
      b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and b.date == ^date
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.any?(&blocks?(&1, start_time, end_time))
  end

  defp blocks?(%AvailabilityBlock{all_day: true}, _start_time, _end_time), do: true

  defp blocks?(%AvailabilityBlock{start_time: block_start, end_time: block_end}, start_time, end_time) do
    overlaps?(block_start, block_end, start_time, end_time)
  end

  defp overlaps_existing_job?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, exclude_job_id) do
    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.scheduled_date == ^date and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> exclude_job(exclude_job_id)
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.any?(&overlaps?(&1.start_time, &1.end_time, start_time, end_time))
  end

  defp exclude_job(query, nil), do: query
  defp exclude_job(query, job_id), do: where(query, [j], j.id != ^job_id)

  defp overlaps?(start_a, end_a, start_b, end_b) do
    Time.compare(start_a, end_b) == :lt and Time.compare(start_b, end_a) == :lt
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.ConflictDetector do
  @moduledoc """
  Detects scheduling conflicts against a cleaner's availability blocks
  and already-booked jobs — for a single proposed assignment, or across
  every occurrence in a recurring series (unsaved, or already
  materialized).

  Two distinct reasons, surfaced separately so the UI can say something
  useful:

    * `:unavailable` — the cleaner has a time-off block covering the slot
    * `:overlap` — the cleaner already has another job booked then

  Availability is checked first: a time-off block is the more specific
  reason when both happen to apply.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{AvailabilityBlock, Job, RecurringPlan}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Checks one proposed (cleaner, date, time window) assignment.

  `opts`:

    * `:exclude_job_id` — omit a job (the one being reassigned) from
      the overlap check against itself
    * `:exclude_recurring_plan_id` — omit every job generated by this
      plan — its own sibling occurrences are not a conflict with each
      other

  Returns `:ok` when the cleaner is `nil` — an unassigned job never
  conflicts.
  """
  def check_assignment(scope, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, opts \\ [])

  def check_assignment(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        cleaner_id,
        %Date{} = date,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        opts
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and not is_nil(cleaner_id) do
    cond do
      unavailable?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) ->
        {:error, :unavailable}

      overlaps_existing_job?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, opts) ->
        {:error, :overlap}

      true ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  def check_assignment(_scope, nil, _date, _start_time, _end_time, _opts), do: :ok

  @doc """
  Checks every occurrence of a plan's series (`[%{index:, date:}, ...]`,
  as returned by `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.occurrences/1`)
  against that plan's preferred cleaner. Works the same whether the
  plan is unsaved (a live preview) or already saved with its jobs
  materialized — in the latter case, the plan's own jobs are excluded
  from the overlap check against themselves. Returns only the
  conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def check_occurrences(_scope, %RecurringPlan{cleaner_id: nil}, _occurrences), do: []

  def check_occurrences(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, occurrences) do
    opts = [exclude_recurring_plan_id: plan.id]

    occurrences
    |> Enum.map(fn %{index: index, date: date} ->
      case check_assignment(scope, plan.cleaner_id, date, plan.start_time, plan.end_time, opts) do
        :ok -> nil
        {:error, reason} -> %{index: index, date: date, reason: reason}
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
  end

  defp unavailable?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) do
    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where(
      [b],
      b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and b.date == ^date
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.any?(&blocks?(&1, start_time, end_time))
  end

  defp blocks?(%AvailabilityBlock{all_day: true}, _start_time, _end_time), do: true

  defp blocks?(%AvailabilityBlock{start_time: block_start, end_time: block_end}, start_time, end_time) do
    overlaps?(block_start, block_end, start_time, end_time)
  end

  defp overlaps_existing_job?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, opts) do
    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.scheduled_date == ^date and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> exclude_job(opts[:exclude_job_id])
    |> exclude_plan(opts[:exclude_recurring_plan_id])
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.any?(&overlaps?(&1.start_time, &1.end_time, start_time, end_time))
  end

  defp exclude_job(query, nil), do: query
  defp exclude_job(query, job_id), do: where(query, [j], j.id != ^job_id)

  defp exclude_plan(query, nil), do: query

  defp exclude_plan(query, plan_id) do
    where(query, [j], is_nil(j.recurring_plan_id) or j.recurring_plan_id != ^plan_id)
  end

  defp overlaps?(start_a, end_a, start_b, end_b) do
    Time.compare(start_a, end_b) == :lt and Time.compare(start_b, end_a) == :lt
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.ConflictDetector do
  @moduledoc """
  Detects scheduling conflicts against a cleaner's availability blocks
  and already-booked jobs — for a single proposed assignment, or across
  every occurrence in a (possibly still-unsaved) recurring series.

  Two distinct reasons, surfaced separately so the UI can say something
  useful:

    * `:unavailable` — the cleaner has a time-off block covering the slot
    * `:overlap` — the cleaner already has another job booked then

  Availability is checked first: a time-off block is the more specific
  reason when both happen to apply.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{AvailabilityBlock, Job}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Checks one proposed (cleaner, date, time window) assignment.

  `exclude_job_id` omits a job (the one being reassigned) from the
  overlap check against itself. Returns `:ok` when the cleaner is
  `nil` — an unassigned job never conflicts.
  """
  def check_assignment(scope, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, exclude_job_id \\ nil)

  def check_assignment(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        cleaner_id,
        %Date{} = date,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        exclude_job_id
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and not is_nil(cleaner_id) do
    cond do
      unavailable?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) ->
        {:error, :unavailable}

      overlaps_existing_job?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, exclude_job_id) ->
        {:error, :overlap}

      true ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  def check_assignment(_scope, nil, _date, _start_time, _end_time, _exclude_job_id), do: :ok

  @doc """
  Checks every occurrence of a proposed series (`[%{index:, date:}, ...]`,
  as returned by `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.occurrences/1`)
  against a single cleaner, using the same visit window for each.
  Returns only the conflicting occurrences, as
  `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def check_occurrences(scope, cleaner_id, occurrences, start_time \\ ~T[09:00:00], end_time \\ ~T[11:00:00])

  def check_occurrences(_scope, nil, _occurrences, _start_time, _end_time), do: []

  def check_occurrences(scope, cleaner_id, occurrences, start_time, end_time) do
    occurrences
    |> Enum.map(fn %{index: index, date: date} ->
      case check_assignment(scope, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) do
        :ok -> nil
        {:error, reason} -> %{index: index, date: date, reason: reason}
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
  end

  defp unavailable?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time) do
    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where(
      [b],
      b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and b.date == ^date
    )
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.any?(&blocks?(&1, start_time, end_time))
  end

  defp blocks?(%AvailabilityBlock{all_day: true}, _start_time, _end_time), do: true

  defp blocks?(%AvailabilityBlock{start_time: block_start, end_time: block_end}, start_time, end_time) do
    overlaps?(block_start, block_end, start_time, end_time)
  end

  defp overlaps_existing_job?(account_id, cleaner_id, date, start_time, end_time, exclude_job_id) do
    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.scheduled_date == ^date and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> exclude_job(exclude_job_id)
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.any?(&overlaps?(&1.start_time, &1.end_time, start_time, end_time))
  end

  defp exclude_job(query, nil), do: query
  defp exclude_job(query, job_id), do: where(query, [j], j.id != ^job_id)

  defp overlaps?(start_a, end_a, start_b, end_b) do
    Time.compare(start_a, end_b) == :lt and Time.compare(start_b, end_a) == :lt
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{AvailabilityBlock, ConflictDetector, Job, Recurrence, RecurringPlan}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    plan
    |> Recurrence.occurrences()
    |> then(
      &ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan.cleaner_id, &1, plan.start_time, plan.end_time)
    )
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    plan
    |> Recurrence.occurrences()
    |> then(
      &ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan.cleaner_id, &1, plan.start_time, plan.end_time)
    )
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

---

                                    mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                    Can be specified multiple times
    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

## Examples

    mix spex
    mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
    mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
    mix spex --verbose
    mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
    mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution
    mix spex --speed medium --verbose  # Medium speed with detailed output
    mix spex --trace            # Show detailed test execution
    mix spex test/spex/file.exs --trace
    mix spex --slowest 5        # Show timing for 5 slowest tests

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7167Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7167 — See the whole week at a glance: the board shows
  every cleaner's jobs for the selected week on one screen.

  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Board` (mounted at `/schedule`,
  per the project's BDD plan) renders a `[data-test='weekly-board']`
  container with one `[data-test='cleaner-column-<id>']` per cleaner,
  each containing `[data-test='job-<id>']` cards for that cleaner's
  jobs. Cleaners are seeded via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`,
  added for this story since no creation flow covers cleaner
  assignment yet.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the owner sees the whole week at a glance" do
    scenario "the board shows all 4 cleaners and their jobs across the week" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the company has 4 cleaners with jobs scheduled this week", context do
        monday = week_monday()

        {cleaners, jobs} =
          ["Ana", "Ben", "Chloe", "Dana"]
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {name, offset} ->
            cleaner =
              Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
                email:
                  "#{String.downcase(name)}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
              })

            client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "#{name}'s client"})

            job =
              Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
                cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
                scheduled_date: Date.add(monday, offset),
                start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
                end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
              })

            {cleaner, job}
          end)
          |> Enum.unzip()

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaners: cleaners, jobs: jobs})}
      end

      when_ "the owner opens the weekly board for that week", context do
        {:ok, view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :view, view)}
      end

      then_ "the board shows all 4 cleaners and their jobs across the seven days on one screen",
            context do
        assert has_element?(context.view, "[data-test='weekly-board']")

        for cleaner <- context.cleaners do
          assert has_element?(
                   context.view,
                   "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{cleaner.id}']",
                   cleaner.email
                 )
        end

        for job <- context.jobs do
          assert has_element?(context.view, "[data-test='job-#{job.id}']")
        end

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp week_monday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7170Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7170 — Reassigning a job to another cleaner on the board
  updates that job's assignment immediately.

  Assumes each job card exposes a per-job cleaner-select control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-cleaner-select']`, `phx-change="reassign_job"`)
  since drag-and-drop isn't drivable through LiveViewTest.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the owner reassigns a job to another cleaner" do
    scenario "moving a job from Ana to Ben updates the assignment" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a Wednesday job is assigned to cleaner Ana", context do
        ana =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        ben =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ben-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Wednesday client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: ana.id,
            scheduled_date: wednesday(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[15:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{ana: ana, ben: ben, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the owner moves the job to cleaner Ben on the board", context do
        {:ok, view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        view
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(context.ben.id)})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :view, view)}
      end

      then_ "the job's assigned cleaner becomes Ben", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ben.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the job no longer appears under Ana", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ana.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp wednesday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    monday = Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
    Date.add(monday, 2)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent

  # Hosts the component in isolation (no router route required), same
  # pattern as ClientLive.PropertyFormComponentTest. Forwards the
  # component's parent notification to the test process so assertions
  # can use `assert_receive`.
  defmodule Host do
    use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

    @impl true
    def mount(_params, session, socket) do
      {:ok,
       assign(socket, %{
         test_pid: session["test_pid"],
         current_scope: session["scope"],
         action: session["action"],
         job: session["job"]
       })}
    end

    @impl true
    def render(assigns) do
      ~H"""
      <.live_component
        module={JobFormComponent}
        id="job-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@action}
        job={@job}
      />
      """
    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({JobFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  describe "creating a job" do
    test "renders the job form with the account's properties" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      assert html =~ "12 Oak Lane"
      assert html =~ "job-form"
    end

    test "creates an unassigned job and notifies the parent" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
        job: %{
          property_id: property.id,
          date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
          start_time: "09:00",
          end_time: "11:00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, %Job{} = job}}
      assert job.property_id == property.id
      assert job.cleaner_id == nil
      assert job.start_time == ~T[09:00:00]
    end

    test "creates a job pre-assigned to a cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
        job: %{
          property_id: property.id,
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
          start_time: "10:00",
          end_time: "12:00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, %Job{} = job}}
      assert job.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "rejects a submission missing the required date" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{property_id: property.id, date: "", start_time: "09:00", end_time: "11:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='job-form']")
      assert html =~ "can't be blank" or html =~ "is required"
    end
  end

  describe "assigning a cleaner to an existing job" do
    test "renders the assignment form" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      job = job_fixture(scope, property)

      {:ok, _lv, html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      assert html =~ "assignment-form"
    end

    test "assigns the cleaner when there is no conflict" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: next_tuesday(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, %Job{} = updated}}
      assert updated.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when the cleaner has a time-off block that day" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      friday = next_friday()

      availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, %{date: friday, all_day: true})

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: friday,
          start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "conflict"
      assert html =~ "unavailable"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when it overlaps another booking for that cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      booking_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)

      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: booking_date,
        start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
      })

      second_job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: booking_date,
          start_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[13:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => second_job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "overlap"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end
  end

  defp next_tuesday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    offset = Integer.mod(2 - Date.day_of_week(today) - 1, 7) + 1
    Date.add(today, offset + 7)
  end

  defp next_friday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    offset = Integer.mod(5 - Date.day_of_week(today) - 1, 7) + 1
    Date.add(today, offset + 7)
  end
end
